correctness.rationale: The independently reconstructed Coxeter graph has 28 vertices, 42 edges, and exactly 196,008 nonempty independent-set simplices. The packaged exact verifier constructs 98,000 Morse pairs and a single critical vertex plus seven critical six-cells. The complete Hasse diagram has 1,319,724 oriented incidences and is exhaustively topologically sorted, proving acyclicity; Forman supplies homology concentration. The signed fixed-simplex Lefschetz formula is proved from orbit signs and computed by integer recursion for all 336 exhaustively enumerated automorphisms. All traces agree with the sign-twisted Sylow-seven augmentation character, with direct oriented-face cross-checks for eight representative types. The character norm is 336/336=1 and group averages establish the stated rational quotient ranks. These are complete finite checks rather than extrapolation; computational scope is exactly the defined graph.

value.rationale: The Coxeter graph is a canonical cubic distance-regular symmetric graph with 336 automorphisms, and its seven-dimensional sixth homology was known only as an ordinary rank. Identifying this topological invariant as the absolutely irreducible sign twist of the eight-Sylow-seven augmentation module is a structural equivariant classification, not a routine Betti number. It determines the full symmetry character and distinguishes rationally acyclic full/even group quotients from a one-dimensional sixth-homology quotient by a Sylow-seven subgroup. This exact natural invariant provides a meaningful boundary on what the known ordinary homotopy theorem determines, without asserting a uniform graph-family theorem.
